Title: AI policy
Justification: Clause 5.2 requires an AI policy; four risks depend on it
How implemented or planned: AI use and governance policy approved and in force

Title: Alignment with other organizational policies
Justification: The AI policy must fit group security, privacy and HR policies
How implemented or planned: AI use policy aligned with the information security policy and group acceptable use, disciplinary and incident processes

Title: Review of the AI policy
Justification: AI systems, models and law change quickly
How implemented or planned: Yearly review, and on any new system, model change, client or EU AI Act change

Title: AI roles and responsibilities
Justification: Accountability for each AI output and system must be named
How implemented or planned: AI Risk Committee approves; named owners per AI system; named approver per output

Title: Reporting of concerns
Justification: Staff must be able to raise AI concerns without fear
How implemented or planned: Same-day reporting route to the Governance and Risk Office

Title: Resource documentation
Justification: The AI system's components must be known to manage them
How implemented or planned: AI system inventory and asset inventory

Title: Data resources
Justification: Answers depend on each client's curated documents and graph
How implemented or planned: Per-client knowledge base and graph recorded as assets with owners

Title: Tooling resources
Justification: Agent tools define what the agents can do
How implemented or planned: Approved tool list; pipeline blocks unlisted tools

Title: System and computing resources
Justification: Regions and services determine residency and availability
How implemented or planned: Regions and services recorded; lab account real, model layer designed

Title: Human resources
Justification: Reviewers' competence decides whether oversight works
How implemented or planned: Reviewer training on automation bias; AI literacy for all staff

Title: AI system impact assessment process
Justification: Required before new systems and before the v2 autonomy roadmap
How implemented or planned: Impact assessment process to be written; the EU AI Act classification covers part of it

Title: Documentation of AI system impact assessments
Justification: Assessments must be recorded and reviewable
How implemented or planned: One record per AI system, kept with the inventory

Title: Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups of individuals
Justification: Wrong answers can mislead bank staff and auditors
How implemented or planned: Impact on client staff, auditors and the banks' customers to be assessed per system

Title: Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
Justification: Limited for internal compliance and operations tools, but must be considered
How implemented or planned: Considered within each impact assessment; expected to be low for v1

Title: Objectives for responsible development of AI system
Justification: Development choices must serve accuracy, separation and oversight
How implemented or planned: Objectives set by the v1 scope reductions: read-only, cited, human-approved

Title: Processes for responsible AI system design and development
Justification: Agents and retrieval are built in-house
How implemented or planned: Design reviews and AI Risk Committee approval before build

Title: AI system requirements and specification
Justification: Each system needs stated limits
How implemented or planned: Purpose, capability, oversight and classification recorded per system

Title: Documentation of AI system design and development
Justification: Design must be traceable for audits
How implemented or planned: Decision records and inventory entries for each design choice

Title: AI system verification and validation
Justification: Unsupported claims and cross-client leakage must be caught before release
How implemented or planned: Citation check, canary documents, seeded faults and red-team cases; tested with fixed sample responses in the lab

Title: AI system deployment
Justification: Deployments must match what was approved
How implemented or planned: Pipeline deploys only inventory-approved tools and models

Title: AI system operation and monitoring
Justification: Quality and reviewer behaviour drift over time
How implemented or planned: Edit and override rates, seeded-fault catch rate, monthly tool diff

Title: AI system technical documentation
Justification: Clients and auditors ask how the systems work
How implemented or planned: Technical description per system, shared with clients under contract

Title: AI system recording of event logs
Justification: Each output must be reconstructable
How implemented or planned: Log what the reviewer saw, the model version, sources and the decision

Title: Data for development and enhancement of AI system
Justification: No model is trained on client data, but retrieval corpora and test sets are built
How implemented or planned: Client data used only for that client's retrieval; never for training or tuning

Title: Acquisition of data
Justification: Documents arrive from clients and public regulators
How implemented or planned: Client data only under contract; regulations from official sources

Title: Quality of data for AI systems
Justification: Outdated regulations or contracts produce wrong answers
How implemented or planned: Curated graph with owners and review dates per source

Title: Data provenance
Justification: Every claim must trace to a source
How implemented or planned: Source, version and date kept for each document and graph entry

Title: Data preparation
Justification: Chunking and tagging decide what can be retrieved
How implemented or planned: Client tag on every chunk; personal data redacted where not needed

Title: System documentation and information for users
Justification: Client staff must know what the AI does and its limits
How implemented or planned: User guide per system: purpose, limits, approval, how to report errors

Title: External reporting
Justification: Clients and regulators may ask for AI reports
How implemented or planned: Periodic AI report to each client's governance forum

Title: Communication of incidents
Justification: AI incidents may trigger DORA and contractual notices
How implemented or planned: AI incidents routed through the incident plan with client timelines

Title: Information for interested parties
Justification: EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency applies
How implemented or planned: Every output labelled AI-drafted and human-approved, naming the approver

Title: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
Justification: Staff use of AI must follow set rules
How implemented or planned: Data-to-tool rules and approval route in the AI use policy

Title: Objectives for responsible use of AI system
Justification: Use must be measurable
How implemented or planned: Targets for reviewer catch rate and zero unapproved tool use

Title: Intended use of the AI system
Justification: Systems must not drift into uses they were not approved for
How implemented or planned: Intended use stated per system; other uses need re-approval and re-classification

Title: Allocating responsibilities
Justification: Sextant, AWS, model providers and clients share responsibility
How implemented or planned: Ownership table in the scope; shared-responsibility terms in contracts

Title: Suppliers
Justification: A single model provider has already failed the lab (F-06)
How implemented or planned: Supplier review of model terms; exit plan and second-provider design

Title: Customers
Justification: Banks need the AI's role, limits and data handling in contract
How implemented or planned: AI role, transparency and DORA terms in each client contract
